memo_rationale: The no-double-charge safeguard is valuable. The deferred-goods addition, however, commingles equipment consideration with the receivables purchase and requires a combined pricing/disclosure analysis. The proposed conservative product design removes deferred equipment from this FRPA and retains a separately elected and invoiced cash purchase; whether equipment itself is required remains to be verified. This is a recommended commercial simplification, not a rule that all deferred equipment arrangements are unlawful. Review the missing lease and subscription agreement before implementation. [A8, A9]
memo_replacement: What is the Equipment Cost? Equipment is purchased or leased under a separate written agreement identifying the equipment, seller or lessor, cash price, taxes, ownership, and any recurring charges. Equipment Cost Deferred in Section 1.3 shall be $0.00. If Merchant elects to purchase equipment for cash, Merchant may separately authorize an itemized deduction from the Purchase Price in Section 1.4; ownership and delivery are governed by the equipment sale agreement. No equipment purchase or lease charge is added to the Purchased Amount or Remaining Balance. Merchant shall not pay both a purchase price and lease payments for the same equipment. Any required equipment or related service charge shall be included in the applicable financing disclosures to the extent required by law.
current_body: What is the Equipment Cost? Point-of-sale equipment may be paid for in one of two ways, and only one. Either the cost is added to the Purchased Amount and repaid through the Specified Percentage (“Equipment Cost Deferred” in Section 1.3), or it is deducted from the Purchase Price at funding (“Less: Equipment fee (paid at funding)” in Section 1.4). Under either, Merchant owns the equipment outright. If either figure is greater than $0.00, Merchant is not asked to lease the same equipment and no monthly lease payment is payable for it. If instead Merchant leases the equipment under a separate Equipment Lease Agreement with {{equipmentAffiliate}}, both figures in Section 1 are stated as $0.00 rather than left blank. In no event does Merchant pay for the same equipment under both this Agreement and an Equipment Lease Agreement.
my_note: The no-double-charge safeguard is worth keeping and the memo says so. But removing deferred equipment from the FRPA is a product decision with revenue consequences, not a compliance fix — it needs the Equipment Lease and Subscription in front of us, and both are unreviewed. Decide after 100/101 clear.

memo_rationale: Delete the categorical exclusion from both finance charge and amount financed. Those are different statutory calculations; an affiliate charge, required charge, or charge incident to financing cannot be excluded merely by calling it a goods price. Determine treatment under each state’s definitions and actual commercial facts. Factor rate alone is not APR. [A8, A9]
memo_replacement: Equipment Cost Deferred shall be $0.00. The Purchased Amount in Section 1.3 equals the Purchase Price multiplied by the Factor Rate, without subsequent equipment or fee additions. Any equipment amount deducted at funding must be separately invoiced, expressly authorized by Merchant, and itemized in Section 1.4. Buyer shall calculate the finance charge, amount financed or funds provided, disbursement amount, and other required disclosure fields under applicable law. No description in this Agreement determines whether a charge is included in or excluded from a statutory disclosure calculation.
current_body: Only one of “Equipment Cost Deferred” in Section 1.3 and “Less: Equipment fee (paid at funding)” in Section 1.4 may be completed with an amount greater than $0.00; the other must be stated as $0.00. The Purchased Amount shown in Section 1.3 is calculated as (Purchase Price × Factor Rate) + Equipment Cost Deferred, and is therefore inclusive of any Equipment Cost Deferred. Because that amount is the price of goods and not a cost of the financing, it is excluded from the finance charge and from the amount financed stated on any state disclosure accompanying this Agreement.
my_note: Unambiguous. You cannot exclude a charge from both finance charge and amount financed by declaring it a goods price — those are two different statutory calculations under NY §803 and CA §22802, and an affiliate charge required as a condition of funding is the textbook inclusion case. Delete the categorical exclusion.

memo_rationale: The legal parties are sufficiently identified in form, but entity status, actual office, merchant identity, state nexus, and Section 1 are unverified. Distinguish signing from transfer/funding. The processor and equipment affiliate are not parties merely because named.
memo_replacement: This Future Receivables Purchase Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of the Effective Date stated in Section 1 by Lombard Capital LLC, a Florida limited liability company (“Buyer”), and the Merchant identified by its full legal name in Section 1 (“Merchant”). Their addresses and operational notice contacts are stated in Section 1. The purchase and transfer of Purchased Receipts take effect only on the Purchase Date under Section 4.13. An Approved Processor, equipment provider, affiliate, broker, or servicer is not a party to this Agreement unless it separately signs in that capacity.
current_body: This Future Receivables Purchase Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into and effective as of ____«31»_____ (the “Effective Date”) by and between {{funder}}, a Florida limited liability company, with its principal office at _______________«96»_______________ (the “Buyer”), and _____________«32»_____________ (the “Merchant” or “Seller”), with reference to the Merchant Information, Deposit Account, Funding Terms, Itemization, and Approved Processors set forth in Section 1 above.
my_note: No objection. Worth pairing with a real entity-verification step at underwriting — the clause cannot cure a wrong party name.

heading: Term of Agreement
memo_rationale: Retain after replacing §2.6; the cross-reference then supplies an indefinite, purchase-only completion rule.
current_body: This Agreement shall continue until the Completion Threshold is attained (Section 2.6).
my_note: Retain, dependent on 013 landing first. If 013 does not land this clause silently re-imports the floating cap by cross-reference.

heading: No Liability
memo_rationale: A commercial consequential-damages waiver is not inherently invalid. This one has no misconduct or non-waivable-right carveout and could be invoked against the very overcollection and data misuse protections being promised. Use a reciprocal, limited waiver; do not cap refund rights.
memo_replacement: To the extent permitted by applicable law, neither party is liable to the other for remote or speculative consequential damages arising solely from an ordinary breach of this Agreement. This limitation does not apply to fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence, unauthorized collection or disclosure, breach of confidentiality or data-security duties, third-party claims covered by an express indemnity, or liability and remedies that applicable law does not permit to be waived. It does not limit return of funds, reconciliation, direct damages, or recovery of amounts wrongfully collected. No punitive or statutory remedy is waived where such waiver would be unenforceable.
current_body: In no event will Buyer be liable for any claims asserted by Merchant or Guarantors under any legal theory for lost profits, lost revenues, lost business opportunities, exemplary, punitive, special, incidental, indirect or consequential damages, each of which is waived by Merchant and Guarantor(s).
my_note: A consequential-damages waiver with no misconduct carve-out could be turned against the overcollection refund we are promising two clauses earlier. Make it reciprocal and carve out the refund.

heading: Power of Attorney
memo_rationale: An irrevocable power triggered by any covenant violation is materially broader than the purchased share. Insurance powers and signing merchant litigation documents increase self-help and evidentiary risk. Retain only a narrow ministerial collection power subject to notice, law, and §6.
memo_replacement: Merchant authorizes Buyer, solely to the extent permitted by law and reasonably necessary to receive Purchased Receipts, to deliver the executed split instruction to an Approved Processor and to endorse an instrument made payable to Buyer and Merchant solely for the purchased share. Buyer shall provide Merchant a copy of any such action promptly. This authority does not permit Buyer to sign pleadings, affidavits, admissions, confessions of judgment, insurance applications, settlement agreements, or new financing documents in Merchant’s name, or to collect Merchant’s retained receipts or unrelated assets. No authority circumvents notice, judicial process, an automatic stay, or the limits in Section 6. It terminates under Section 2.6.
current_body: Merchant irrevocably appoints Buyer as its agent and attorney-in-fact with full authority to take any action or execute any instrument or document in the case of a violation by Merchant of any term of this Agreement or the occurrence of an Event of Default, including without limitation: (i) to obtain and adjust insurance; (ii) to collect monies due or to become due under or in respect of any of the Collateral; (iii) to receive, endorse and collect any checks, notes, drafts, instruments, documents or chattel paper in connection with clauses (i) or (ii) above; (iv) to sign Merchant’s name on any invoice, bill of lading, or assignment directing customers or account debtors to make payment directly to Buyer; and (v) to file any claims or take any action or institute any proceeding which Buyer may deem necessary for the collection of any of the unpaid Purchased Amount from the Collateral, or otherwise to enforce its rights with respect to payment of the Purchased Amount.
my_note: An irrevocable power of attorney triggered by any covenant violation, reaching insurance and merchant litigation documents, is the self-help problem in one clause. Narrow to a ministerial collection power. I would rate this Critical, not High.

heading: D/B/A Names
memo_rationale: A secured-party trade name is not categorically invalid under Article 9, and this record does not prove a DBA is unregistered. Still, a contract cannot cure misidentification or local assumed-name requirements. Use the actual legal owner; do not substitute the equipment affiliate. [A7]
memo_replacement: Buyer shall identify itself in notices and filings as Lombard Capital LLC. Any additional trade name must be lawfully used and must not obscure the legal identity of Buyer or an actual assignee. No affiliate may be named as owner or secured party unless it has lawfully acquired the relevant interest and Merchant receives notice under Section 7.2.
current_body: Merchant acknowledges that Buyer may use “doing business as” or “d/b/a” names in connection with various matters relating to the transaction, including the filing of UCC-1 financing statements and other notices or filings.
my_note: Fourth REFUTATION: a secured-party trade name is not categorically invalid under Article 9 and nothing in the record proves the DBA is unregistered. So the finding is wrong and the clause change is near-cosmetic. The real action is a filing audit — pull the actual UCC-1s and confirm the named secured party — which is operations, not drafting.

heading: Security Interest
memo_rationale: Article 9 applies to sales of accounts; calling the interest precautionary does not replace attachment, filing, or priority analysis. The first paragraph is helpfully narrow, but a guarantor who owns no collateral cannot grant Merchant’s assets. A covenant cannot eliminate an existing lender’s lien or processor setoff. Limit the filing and require actual searches, releases, or subordinations. [A7]
memo_replacement: To evidence and perfect the sale, Merchant grants Buyer an Article 9 interest solely in the Purchased Receipts and their identifiable proceeds, limited in each underlying receivable to the Specified Percentage sold. “Collateral” means only that interest and those proceeds. No lien is granted on Merchant’s retained share, equipment, inventory, general intangibles, or unrelated assets, or on a Guarantor’s property. Merchant authorizes financing statements accurately describing that limited Collateral and its proper legal debtor name. Filing, perfection, and priority are governed by the mandatory choice-of-law rules of applicable Article 9. Buyer shall conduct its own priority diligence and obtain necessary releases or subordinations before funding; Merchant does not guarantee first priority against interests disclosed to Buyer or arising by law. A deposit-account control agreement, if separately negotiated, may not authorize collection beyond this Agreement. Enforcement is subject to Sections 6 and 9 and applicable bankruptcy law. Buyer shall release its interest under Section 2.6. Expenses are governed solely by Section 6.3.
current_body:
To secure Merchant’s payment and performance obligations under this Agreement, Merchant hereby grants Buyer a security interest in: (a) the Receipts purchased under this Agreement and the accounts and other receivables from which those Receipts arise, as those terms are defined by Article 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code (the “UCC”); and (b) all identifiable proceeds of the foregoing, as defined by Article 9 of the UCC, including identifiable proceeds on deposit in the Approved Bank Account (collectively, the “Collateral”). This security interest is precautionary and is limited to the purchased Receipts and their proceeds. It does not extend to Merchant’s equipment, inventory, chattel paper, documents, instruments or general intangibles, and Buyer shall not file any financing statement purporting to reach them.
Merchant and Guarantor each agree to execute any documents or take any action Buyer deems necessary to perfect or maintain Buyer’s first-priority security interest in the Collateral, including the execution of any account control agreements. Merchant and Guarantor authorize Buyer to file any financing statements deemed necessary by Buyer. Merchant and Guarantor shall be liable for, and Buyer may charge and collect, the reasonable costs and expenses, including reasonable attorneys’ fees, actually incurred by Buyer in protecting, preserving, and enforcing Buyer’s security interest, subject to the aggregate limit in Section 6.3. Buyer may use another legal name or D/B/A when designating the Secured Party in such filings.
my_note: Article 9 applies to sales of accounts; 'precautionary' does not substitute for attachment, filing and priority. And a guarantor who owns no collateral cannot grant the merchant's assets — that is a drafting error, not a policy choice. I would rate this Critical.

heading: Negative Pledge
memo_rationale: The guarantor undertaking and equipment-payment “ranking” confuse asset ownership and settlement priority. Limit this to a knowing double sale or conflicting voluntary lien on the exact purchased share. A lease payment is not made subordinate to third parties simply by calling it a permitted claim.
memo_replacement: Merchant shall not knowingly sell the same Purchased Receipts twice or voluntarily grant a conflicting interest in the Purchased Receipts without Buyer’s written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld where Buyer’s purchased share remains protected. This restriction does not reach Merchant’s retained receipts or other assets, disclosed existing interests, statutory liens, or ordinary processor charges. Equipment and subscription charges are separate obligations and have no lien or priority by reason of this Agreement. Guarantor grants no lien and undertakes no separate negative pledge.
current_body: Merchant and Guarantor each agrees not to create, incur, assume, or permit to exist, directly or indirectly, any lien on or with respect to any of the Collateral other than the security interest granted to Buyer and the monthly Equipment payment billed at merchant level by the Approved Processor under an Equipment Lease Agreement between Merchant and {{equipmentAffiliate}}, which is a permitted claim ranking after the Specified Percentage. This Section does not restrict Merchant from granting a lien on any asset that is not Collateral.
my_note: The guarantor undertaking and the equipment-payment 'ranking' confuse asset ownership with settlement priority. Limit to a knowing double sale or a conflicting voluntary lien on the exact sold share.

heading: Timing and Method of Funding
memo_rationale: An unlimited right to revoke a specific offer conflicts with Connecticut’s protected offer period when applicable. More generally, the merchant should not be locked into processing and UCC burdens while Buyer remains wholly uncommitted. Use stated conditions, a funding deadline, and no transfer before consideration. Connecticut’s three-day offer rule is distinct from the contractual post-funding cancellation right. [A10]
memo_replacement: Before Merchant accepts, Buyer shall state the offer-expiration time, any objective outstanding funding conditions, and the latest funding date in Section 1. Buyer shall honor any period during which applicable law prohibits withdrawal or modification of a specific offer, including Connecticut General Statutes Section 36a-869 when applicable. Following acceptance and satisfaction of the disclosed conditions, Buyer shall provide the Purchase Price by the agreed funding date using the authorized payment method. “Purchase Date” means the date Buyer delivers the Net Amount Funded to Merchant, completes each expressly authorized third-party disbursement or prior-Buyer settlement credit, and applies only the lawful itemized deductions agreed in Section 1. Purchase Price is the gross agreed consideration; Net Amount Funded is the actual cash delivered after those itemized deductions and disbursements. Buyer-retained deductions need not circulate through Merchant’s account, but must be earned, lawful, and fully disclosed. Buyer shall notify Merchant promptly of a lawful withdrawal or failed condition and the reason. If Buyer does not timely fund, Merchant may terminate without charge; Buyer shall stop instructions and release any filing made in anticipation of this purchase.
current_body: Merchant and Buyer agree that Buyer shall purchase the Receipts on a date to be determined by Buyer in its sole discretion (the “Purchase Date”). Buyer, in its sole discretion, may refuse to purchase the Receipts for any reason or no reason. Buyer shall provide payment through any commercially reasonable method, at Buyer’s sole discretion, including check, federal funds wire, or ACH transfer.
my_note: An unlimited right to revoke a specific offer collides with Connecticut's protected offer period, and independently it is bad faith to bind a merchant into processing changes and UCC filings while we remain uncommitted. Stated conditions plus a funding deadline.
